rows: GATE eligibility

GATE (Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering) is open to engineering-degree holders and is the direct entry requirement into IIT/IISc M.Tech admissions and most PSU technical recruitment. A BSc or BCA graduate does not qualify for GATE the same way.
PSU technical recruitment

Public-sector undertakings hiring for engineer-designated technical posts commonly require a recognised engineering degree by name, closing that specific door to non-engineering computing graduates regardless of skill.
Certain core-engineering-adjacent roles
Roles that sit at the boundary of software and hardware/embedded systems sometimes prefer or require an engineering degree specifically, even when the day-to-day work is heavily software-based.

blocks.heading: Honest Campus-Placement Picture By College Tier
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: The honest campus-placement picture by college tier

rows: IITs, NITs, and top-tier private engineering colleges

The strongest placement outcomes on this list, with product-company and top-tier service-company recruiters visiting campus directly. Even here, outcomes vary sharply by individual skill and interview preparation, not degree alone.
Mid-tier private engineering colleges

Placement quality varies enormously college to college. Service-company hiring is common; product-company hiring usually requires the student to build a portfolio and apply directly rather than relying on campus placement alone.
Lower-tier or newer private engineering colleges
Campus placement support is often weakest here, which is exactly why building an independent project portfolio and applying directly matters most for students at this tier, not less.

Product-company hire via direct application and strong portfolio (any college tier)
Roughly Rs 6-15+ LPA, driven far more by demonstrated skill than college tier alone
Top-tier college campus placement (IIT/NIT/leading private)
Roughly Rs 8-25+ LPA, with the widest spread of any route on this list
PSU technical recruitment (post-GATE)
Follows the standard PSU pay scale for the specific post, stable and benefits-rich rather than fast-growing
M.Tech (post-GATE) then industry or research
Typically a meaningful premium over a bachelor's-only hire at the same company, concentrated in specialised technical and R&D roles
